title: Operator-facing fidelity triage & admission gateway for overload scenarios
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Problem: During recent cross-region capacity saturation tests and a production incident on 2026-02-10, high tail latency and token-cost spikes were traced to undifferentiated admission behavior. We need an operator-visible triage layer that permits fine-grained admission decisions per-tenant and per-route, exposes graceful degradation modes, and plugs into circuit-breakers and multi-region failover policies.

Goal: Build an admission gateway feature that: (1) enforces priority queues with pluggable admission policies, (2) supports soft degradation modes (response trimming, model-variant fallback, early-stop tokens, structured short-circuits), (3) emits SLO-aligned telemetry and exposes operator controls in Console for live overrides, and (4) integrates with existing circuit-breaker components so failover/drain events trigger safe, observable degradations rather than hard rejects.

Acceptance criteria:
- Admission gateway deployed behind the runtime LB in canary region, with feature-flag control.
- Priority queue semantics implemented: strict-priority + proportional-reserve lanes + preemption window.
- Soft-degradation actions configurable per-policy and per-tenant; at least: (a) model-variant fallback, (b) prefix trimming, (c) response-length cap with safe truncation.
- End-to-end dashboards showing per-tenant admission rate, shed-rate, degraded-rps, and SLO burn.
- Runbook additions and a checklist for operator-triggered manual overrides.
notes: 2026-02-24 - Lina Chen: Initial discovery doc and post-incident notes attached. Root cause sketch: queue collapse when high-cost long-context requests collide with burst traffic from background batch jobs in eu-west-1. Filed ENG-702345 to scope operator-facing admission controls.

2026-02-26 - Rohit Patel: Spike prototype for admission gateway bootstrapped. Created local simulation harness that replicates mixed-latency workloads and tenant weights. Basic strict-priority queue + token bucket implemented in the runtime agent. Repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842

2026-03-01 - Design review with PM (Ava Martinez) and SRE (Diego Ruiz). Trade-offs discussed: (a) strict preemption vs. probabilistic shedding — we will implement both but default to probabilistic to avoid priority inversion-induced starvation, (b) run-time policy complexity vs. operator ergonomics — plans for a small set of templated policies plus freeform JSON for advanced ops.

2026-03-04 - Added circuit-breaker hook: when regional latency SLO exceeds threshold for 60s, gateway will start model-variant fallback and enable response trimming at 10% initial ramp. This integrates with ENG-902111 multi-region failover signals. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1917

2026-03-07 - Telemetry schema finalized with Observability team: emit metrics admission_attempts, admission_denied, admission_degraded, degrade_action_{fallback,trim,truncate}, preemptions, queue_depth_by_lane. Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.prod/d/ab12c5/admission-gateway-overview

2026-03-09 - Load test: ran a 4-hour mixed-burst test in staging with canary policy. Results: reduced 99.9th latency by 28% for P0 lanes, shed-rate stabilized at 6% overall, customer-visible error rate unchanged. Notes: edge-case where long-live streaming sessions bypassed queue; follow-up task filed to enforce stream admission tokenization.

2026-03-12 - Security review: no new data-plane surface introduced; policy storage uses existing encrypted config store. Ops requested RBAC checks for manual override; scheduled as follow-up (ENG-709001).
design_decisions: Default to probabilistic shedding for low-priority tenants to reduce risk of complete starvation of background workloads.
Implement small set of curated degradation actions (fallback->trim->truncate) to simplify operator choices and testing matrix.
Expose per-tenant override in Console behind feature flag with audit events for every manual change.
Integrate gateway with circuit-breaker signals so the gateway can transition to 'degenerate mode' before full failover to remote region.
Prefer runtime-local policy evaluation (no external policy lookups on hot path) to keep admission latency bounded.
Metric-driven canary: enable degradations at 1% of traffic, monitor SLO burn and customer-visible errors, then ramp to 10% and 50% before full rollout.
implementation_notes: Key modules: admission_router, lane_scheduler, degrade_action_executor, cb_integration (circuit-breaker hook)
Policy format: YAML templates with 'lanes', 'weights', 'degrade_chain' and 'preemption_window_ms'. Example template stored in repo under docs/policies/safe-default.yaml
Testing: extended synthetic harness to validate starvation scenarios and degradation correctness. Added unit tests for trim/truncate and fallback selection logic.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Operator overrides could mask underlying capacity issues. Mitigation: require two-person sign-off for overrides that disable automated degradations for >15 minutes (Console audit trail + email).
Risk: Incorrect truncation may produce malformed structured output. Mitigation: implement safe truncation logic aware of JSON/structured tokens and add automatic fuzz tests against eval prompt sets.
Risk: Latency on policy evaluation path. Mitigation: cache resolved policies in-memory with TTL and validate via unit tests and load testing.
test_plan: Unit tests for queue promotion, preemption, and probabilistic shedding logic.
Integration test: simulated mixed-tenant traffic in the staging cluster with injected slow-model backends.
Chaos test: toggle circuit-breaker signals to verify gateway transitions to degenerate mode without all-or-nothing failures.
Canary rollout: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with SLO guards at each step.
Post-deploy eval: run end-to-end eval suite (latency, cost per token, and quality regression on held prompt set).
next_steps: Merge canary PR and deploy to eu-west-1 canary pool (Rohit)
Add RBAC controls for manual override and wire audit events (follow-up ENG-709001)
Complete console UI for per-tenant policy templates (Design: DES-4123)
Run extended 24-hour soak test and collect SLO burn charts (SRE)
Document final runbook and schedule operator training session.
